correctness.rationale: The active set remains connected from a singleton seed in a tree. Every unseeded vertex of degree at least three has at most one active neighbor and so is blocked; all degree≤2 path components adjacent to the seed propagate. Hence exact sum S=|H|+Σ(m_j²+b_j m_j), S≥2n−|H|, |H|≤floor((n−2)/2) by the tree degree sum. Equality forces singleton pendant low-degree components and the maximal number of hubs, producing the stated degree signatures. Construct by adding leaves to any hub tree. Path case S=n². The packaged checker exhaustively compares 984 unlabeled trees of orders 4–12 and 11,000 seeded cascades.

originality.rationale: Known vulnerable-node and random-graph cascade theorems are not asserted new. The claimed contribution is the sharp minimum of a uniformly sampled one-seed mean among all finite order-n tree topologies, with every optimizer characterized. Inspected primary sources investigate random ensemble averages, dynamic finite random graphs or targeted influence maximization; none supplies the asserted order-uniform tree extremum. Search noncoverage is not uniqueness proof; possibility of prior finite-tree optimization remains.
residual_risks: The basic one-neighbor vulnerability mechanism is explicitly present in Watts (2002); an unnoticed article might already optimize it on deterministic trees.

Published literature on finite threshold cascades, branching tree topologies or degree sequences may contain a stronger general extremum; semantic and web searches were not an exhaustive bibliography.
A primary author applying fixed threshold strictness (rather than inclusive one-half) would produce a different model and is not covered by the statement.

value.rationale: The claim answers a natural social-network design question with an exact, all-orders optimum and complete topology classification under unknown uniformly sampled initiator. It shows that maximally many trivalent branching hubs (and a single four-valent hub at odd sizes) minimize diffusion, identifies the non-star effect and an asymptotic lower bound 3/2. It requires the full dynamical component identity and equality-case structural argument, not simply a small-graph numerical observation.
